title: Predictive spill-to-host memory policy and batch window prioritization
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Intermittent OOMs during high-concurrency streaming workloads are caused by bursty KV growth and long-lived prefixes entering the GPU working set. Current eviction-first strategies can spike tail latency and drop active prefix state. Goal: introduce a predictive spill-to-host policy coupled with prioritized batch admission windows and lightweight KV continuity checkpoints to avoid OOMs without large latency regressions.
acceptance_criteria: 1) No customer-visible OOMs for the benchmarked conversational workload at 2x baseline QPS for 72h; 2) P95 token latency increase <= 10% vs baseline under sustained load; 3) Successful automated recovery flow exercised in CI that spills and restores KV snapshots without manual intervention; 4) Telemetry surfaces spill events, reclaimed memory, and restored snapshot success/failure rate.
design_notes:
- Predictive memory fingerprint: instrument per-request incremental delta estimator to predict near-term GPU growth (windowed by 1s and 10s).
- Spill targets: identify cold KV segments using recent-access scoring and produce mini-snapshots atomically streamed to host memory (pinned pages) with a CRC to verify restore.
- Batch window prioritization: introduce prioritized admission queues (low/medium/high) where high-priority interactive requests can reserve small 'memory credits' that avoid being preempted by bulk batches.
- Probabilistic preemption: when predictor indicates >80% memory pressure within window, block new bulk batch admissions and start spilling cold segments progressively (not full evict).
- Restore path: on segment restore, replay compacted deltas into KV cache and validate with checksums; if restore fails, automatically route to compatible smaller model variant (quantized or CPU-backed) and redact telemetry trace for further triage.
- KV continuity checkpoints: create lightweight checkpoints per model shard every N minutes (configurable) for fast partial restore; use copy-on-write semantics to avoid blocking online inference.
- Safety knobs: config flags for max spill rate, min memory reserved for interactive QoS, and a circuit-breaker to throttle all non-interactive batches for SLA-bound customers.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): implement predictor and telemetry, enable passive spill metrics on 5% of traffic in staging. Phase 2 (internal): enable active spill-to-host on internal Dedicated fleet during low-traffic window for 48h. Phase 3 (customer canary): opt-in for enterprise customers on dedicated pools with runtime-1.20. Phase 4 (GA): enable by default with conservative knobs and telemetry alerts. Rollback: disable spill agent and fall back to existing eviction policy; automatic fallback to smaller model variant on repeated restore failures.
test_plan: Unit tests for predictor math and checksum paths. End-to-end suite that replays production request traces with injected KV-hot prefixes to validate spill/restore correctness. Chaos job: random host OOM and host I/O slowdowns to validate restore and fallback. Add synthetic SLO tests for P50/P95/P99 latency under mixed priority traffic. CI job must simulate checkpointing and validate no inference state leak.
metrics:
- spill_events_total
- spilled_bytes_total
- restore_success_ratio
- restore_latency_ms_p50/p95
- p95_token_latency_by_priority
- customer_oom_incidents
- model-fallback-count
updates: 2025-02-11 - Initial design spike complete. Baseline predictor (EWMA delta) reduces false positives vs naive growth estimator.
2025-02-13 - Security reviewed restore channel; no plaintext secrets transferred. KMS usage for snapshot integrity noted as future work.
2025-02-17 - Prototype implemented: mini-snapshot writer to host and loader tested locally with 0.3% restore failure on pathological traces. Added CRC check and retry loop.
2025-02-20 - UX/PM sync: expose per-customer QoS tokens and opt-in toggle in Console under Dedicated pool settings. PM requested retention of spill telemetry for 90 days for auditability.

2025-02-24 - Performance testing: when enabled in active spill mode, P95 token latency for high-priority lane increased by ~6% at 2x load; bulk throughput reduced by ~12% — acceptable trade-off for avoiding OOMs. Observability dashboards committed.
2025-02-27 - Code review feedback from @Aisha Patel: make spill writer non-blocking and add backpressure metrics; @Rafael Gomes asked for clearer rollback criteria and automation for model fallback.
2025-02-27 - Next: address CR comments, add CI synthetic chaos test, and schedule canary run on internal fleet for 2025-03-03.
